sourceScript.title: The Adventure Begins
sourceScript.activatedBy: Julian explicit no-pollen-bags direction, applied by Codex

directorStatement.audienceFeeling: Keen feels tiny in open water, then funny and capable for a moment, then frightened when the storm removes his map, and finally relieved when he chooses to follow Squeaky.
directorStatement.whoseScene: Keen’s scene, with Squeaky as the visible companion who first plays beside him and later gives him a direction to follow.
directorStatement.emotionalChange: Keen moves from performed confidence, to comic uncertainty, to panic, to a small steadying breath, to trusting Squeaky’s lead.
directorStatement.theLaugh: Keen confidently names Squeaky and then treats an upside-down map as enough information to be going in “one of the directions.”
directorStatement.visualSurprise: The friendly open water turns into a storm fast enough to swallow the horizon and snatch the map away.
directorStatement.carryForward: Keen is still in rough weather, without the map, following Squeaky through the storm.

shots.purpose: Make the empty sea feel enormous, turn Squeaky into Keen's first companion, then let Keen's confident map-reading reveal that he has no idea where he is going.
shots.performanceAssignment: Shot 1: the small sailboat travels left-to-right across endless blue water. Keen performs confidence while making quick balance corrections. Squeaky surfaces at screen-right, keeps pace, and chatters; Keen greets him, listens, names him, and the friendship lands in one shared look. Shot 2: without resetting the boat or screen direction, Squeaky makes one playful leap while Keen laughs and lifts the map from the boat. Keen checks the map, looks over the bow, checks it again, rotates it upside down, then peeks over its edge and completes the directions joke. The boat keeps travelling throughout.
shots.camera: Open wide with the boat small against endless water, starboard side and left-to-right travel. Push to a warm medium two-shot for the naming beat. Cut on Squeaky's leap to a medium on Keen, then push toward the upside-down map while Squeaky remains readable at screen-right. Preserve the same boat, travel axis, sail, cargo and open-water light.
shots.openingPose: Keen stands center-left in the boat with one hand lightly on the tiller and the other beginning to lift; Squeaky is just below the surface at screen-right with ripples rising where the next pop-up will happen.
shots.dialogueBinding: Keen speaks all four lines in order; Squeaky answers only with dolphin chatter and never forms human words.

dialogueLines.exactText: Hi! I’m Keen! Nice to meet you, Squeaky!
dialogueLines.delivery: Bright greeting, slightly breathy from balancing on the boat; friendly and proud of the new name.

dialogueLines.speaker: Keen
dialogueLines.exactText: Squeaky. Perfect. You really do sound squeaky.
dialogueLines.delivery: Satisfied and matter-of-fact, with a small nod on “Perfect.”

dialogueLines.speaker: Keen
dialogueLines.exactText: Okay… so if this is north… then I am definitely going…
dialogueLines.delivery: Quiet reasoning aloud, slowing as the map stops helping.

dialogueLines.speaker: Keen
dialogueLines.delivery: Small, sheepish confidence; the pause before the line lets the upside-down map read first.

shots.visualPayoff: Keen holds the map visibly upside down, peeks over it toward the open water and lands 'one of the directions' while Squeaky keeps pace beside the moving boat.

shots.purpose: Let the storm dismantle Keen's performed control in one escalating cause-and-effect run, ending with the map gone and Keen finally admitting that he is lost.
shots.performanceAssignment: Shot 1: continue from the upside-down-map landing. A hard gust loads the sail, the boat heels and rocks, and Keen slides, grabs the mast and yelps. The light falls, rain builds from drops to sheets, and Squeaky dives below the rough water and disappears. Shot 2: Keen tries to steer with one hand and clamp the map with the other. A stronger gust visibly catches the map and tears it from his fingers; he reaches and calls after it. Shot 3: match Keen's reach as the boat drops beneath him. His hand closes on empty rain; the map vanishes into the grey. He regains his feet, sees that the horizon has gone, lets the loss register, and admits that he is lost.
shots.camera: Begin medium on Keen, map and sail from the established starboard side. Jolt with the first heel, then widen to reveal darkening sky, rough water and Squeaky's disappearance. Track the stolen map toward screen-right, cut at maximum reach, and tighten slowly on Keen only after the map and horizon have both disappeared.
shots.openingPose: Keen stands center-left with both hands on the upside-down map at chest height, knees flexed; the sail is just beginning to pull hard from an incoming gust at screen-right, and Squeaky is still visible near the waterline.
shots.cutInMotivation: The slight dimming at the end of the map joke becomes the incoming gust; the cut lands on the sail beginning to pull hard.
shots.dialogueBinding: Keen speaks all three lines; Squeaky remains wordless and exits underwater.

shots.purpose: Turn Keen's fear into a small act of self-regulation, then let Squeaky's return give him a choice: accept help and steer toward trust.
shots.performanceAssignment: Shot 1: continue with Keen alone in the same storm. A distant lightning flicker makes him grip the boat edge. His shoulders show quick breaths; he closes his eyes, takes one slower breath, repeats his brave phrase, and settles only slightly. Shot 2: Squeaky's offscreen clicking makes Keen open his eyes and turn before Squeaky appears. Squeaky leaps beside the hull, dives, resurfaces farther ahead and repeatedly indicates a clear screen-right route. Keen questions him, studies the water, meets Squeaky's eyeline, decides, and nods. Shot 3: Keen answers with growing resolve, braces his feet and hauls the tiller. The bow pivots under water resistance and the sail remains wind-loaded as the boat follows Squeaky rather than sliding sideways.
shots.camera: Ride the established starboard-side boat motion in a steadier medium close while Keen breathes. Let Squeaky's chatter bridge into a pan toward screen-right, then widen to show Squeaky leading and the bow physically turning after him. End with both characters' motivated eyelines and a readable forward route through the storm.
shots.openingPose: Keen stands frozen at center of the boat with arms lowered and fingers beginning to curl upward toward the edge as distant lightning starts to flicker behind the rain.
shots.cutInMotivation: Reaction continuation from Keen’s frozen admission; the next visible change is the lightning flicker and his hands moving to grip the boat.
shots.dialogueBinding: Keen speaks all three lines. Squeaky uses only clicks and chirps; his mouth never forms human words.
